newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler's Schrempp to cut top jobs - report.
newsitem.headline: Daimler's Schrempp to cut top jobs - report.

text.p: German industrial giant Daimler Benz AG plans to cut jobs at management level to speed up decision-making processes and improve efficiency, a report in German magazine Der Spiegel said on Sunday.

According to an advance summary of an article to appear in Monday's edition, Daimler's chairman Juergen Schrempp told the company's works council that Daimler employs 500 too many at management level.
He added that cuts at the top end of the employee scale would speed up decision-making processes and would lead to cost-savings of 1.2 billion marks annually, the article said.
A spokesman for the company confirmed that Schrempp had outlined plans for the further development of the company to the works council in recent weeks, but would not give any figures.

An internal study by Daimler shows that it employs more management personnel than other leading German companies. 0.65 percent of personnel work at senior management level, compared to 0.35 percent at other leading companies.
The spokesman said that structural changes at the company would lead to shorter decision-making processes and more efficient management.
Daimler's supervisory board is due to make a decision on changes in the group's overall management structure at the end of January 1997.
Among topics for discussion then is the closer integration of the group's car-making unit Mercedes Benz into the group.
